Tosafot on Bava Batra 118b:10:1.hebrew: ולמאן דאמר לבאי הארץ תרי אחי דאבא הוו להו - משמע כולה סוגיא דלמאן דאמר לבאי הארץ, שלא נטלו כלום מחמת צלפחד עצמו, אלא מחמת חפר אבי אביהן. ותימה: אם כן, מאי קאמר "והוא לא היה בתוך העדה הנועדים וגו'"? מאי נפקא מינה שלא היה בעדתם? אפילו היה, היו נוטלין על ידי חזרה! דהא אמרינן לעיל: בני מרגלים ובני מתלוננים נחלו בזכות אבי אביהן ובזכות אבי אמותיהן. ואין לפרש דנ"מ לענין חלק בכורה, דהא כי היכי דשקלי חלק פשיטות, אע"ג דבא להן מכח אביהן, ה"נ יטלו חלק בכורה. ועוד קשה לרשב"א: למ"ד לבאי הארץ, היכי קאמר לעיל "מרגלים — יהושע וכלב נטלו חלקם"? והלא לא היה להם חלק בארץ כלל, לכל אותן שלא באו בארץ! וכ"ת: נטלו מה שהגיע להן על ידי חזרה מבניהם שבאו לארץ — הא ליתא, דאמרינן לקמן דבניהן שהיו בני עשרים נטלו בזכות עצמן. ורשב"ם פי' דלמ"ד דלבאי הארץ, לא נטלו מידי יהושע וכלב מחלק מרגלים, ומפרש "חיו מן האנשים" — ממש חיו, כפשטיה:
Tosafot on Bava Batra 118b:10:1.english: And according to the one who says [the land was divided] among those who entered the land, they had two brothers of their father - The entire passage implies that, according to the one who says [that it was divided] among those who entered the land, [the daughters of Zelophehad] received nothing by virtue of Zelophehad himself, but rather by virtue of Hepher, their father's father. And this is puzzling: If so, what is [the verse] saying, "And he was not among the company who gathered together, etc."? What difference does it make that he was not in their company? Even if he had been, they would have received [a share] by way of reversion! For we said above: The descendants of the spies and the descendants of the complainers inherited by virtue of their father's father and by virtue of their mothers' fathers. And one cannot explain that the difference [nafka minah] is with regard to the firstborn's share, for just as they took an ordinary share, even though it came to them through their father, so too they should take a firstborn's share. Furthermore, the Rashba raises a difficulty: According to the one who says [it was divided] among those who entered the land, how does it say above, "Regarding the spies — Joshua and Caleb took their share"? Surely they had no share in the land at all, [like] all those who did not enter the land! And if you say that they took what came to them by way of reversion from their sons who entered the land — that is not so, for we say below that their sons who were twenty years old took [shares] by virtue of themselves. And the Rashbam explained that according to the one who says [it was divided] among those who entered the land, Joshua and Caleb took nothing from the share of the spies, and he explains "[they] lived of those men" as meaning that they actually lived, in its plain sense:

Tosafot on Bava Batra 118b:12:1.hebrew: ולמאן דאמר תרי אחי דאבא הוו להו ההוא מאחוזת נחלה נפקא - קשיא לריב"ם: אפילו למאן דאמר חד אחא דאבא הוה להו, נמי מאחוזת נחלה נפקא לרבנן דלא דרשי "נתון תתן", ולר"א דדריש "נתון תתן" לא צריך לאחוזת נחלה — אפילו למאן דאמר תרי אחי דאבא הוו! דהא למאן דאמר לבאי הארץ הוא דאית ליה דתרי אחי דאבא הוו, וההוא לא דריש "נתון תתן להם נחלה" לחלק אביהם, דלדידיה לא היה שום חלק; ולדרוש מיניה חד אחא, ואידך מ"נתון תתן", כדדריש ראב"י:
Tosafot on Bava Batra 118b:12:1.english: "And according to the one who says that their father had two brothers, that [second brother] is derived from 'achuzat nachalah' (a hereditary holding)" - This is difficult for the Rivam: Even according to the one who says that their father had [only] one brother, [that brother] is also derived from "achuzat nachalah" according to the Rabbis, who do not expound "nato titen" ("you shall surely give"); and according to R. Eliezer, who does expound "nato titen," there is no need for "achuzat nachalah" — even according to the one who says that their father had two brothers! For it is only the one who says [the land was divided] among those who came into the Land who holds that their father had two brothers, and he does not expound "nato titen... nachalah" [as referring] to their father's share, since according to him there was no share at all [for their father]; and [so] to expound from it ["achuzat nachalah"] one brother, and the other from "nato titen," as R. Eliezer son of Jacob expounds.
